svg.title: Levels of Conflict
svg.desc: A3 landscape coach's board for diagnosing team conflict with Speed Leas's five levels: what you see and hear at each level, the coach's move for each, what the conflict is about, questions to ask before stepping in, and an agreed next step.
svg.text: Notice how far a conflict has gone, then choose a response that fits, from letting the team solve it to stepping in.
Facilitate & Coach · Five Levels of Conflict (Speed B. Leas) · via Lyssa Adkins, Coaching Agile Teams
Different views, shared goal. Information is
shared openly; people focus on the problem.
Facilitate, then let the team solve it.
Help them reach a decision together.
Self-protection creeps in. People keep their
distance and talk in general terms.
Coach them to resolve it themselves;
make sure each side is heard.
Winning matters more than solving. Sides
form, facts get distorted, it gets personal.
Get back to facts and interests;
Protecting one's own group. Positions harden
into principles; the other side is the problem.
Bring in a neutral third party;
talk with each group separately first.
Destroy the other side. Little talk, open
Separate the parties and escalate now:
HR or leadership, not the team.
Is this mine to act on, or the team's to solve?
Am I neutral? If not, who is?
Have I heard each side on their own?
Can the team use its own working agreements?
Would naming the level help the team see it?
Is anyone at risk of harm?
don't mediate. Go to HR or your leadership straight away.
“What words are people using, and what level do they point to?”
“Is this conflict about the work, or about each other?”
Facilitate & Coach · Conflict · Healthy Disagreement, Early Help
